page: Amazon Web Services c3.large is a compute-optimized, third-generation server instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor. It is configured with an i386 CPU architecture featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes hyper-threading, 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 25 MB of L3 cache. It supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX) and AES hardware cryptography. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.88 GB per core, and includes 32 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. There is no GPU hardware, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of the c3.large in the lower tiers of modern cloud infrastructure. In CPU testing, the stress-ng single-core benchmark scored 1263.58, while the multi-core score reached 1640.98. Memory bandwidth tests show poor throughput, with read-only small block cached memory at 95.48 GB/sec and large block uncached read and write speeds at 13.06 GB/sec and 11.39 GB/sec respectively. Geekbench testing reflects similar constraints, with a single-core score of 702.0 and a multi-core score of 812.0. Software compilation with Clang scored 1536.0, and static web serving throughput reached 1.81 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10% of benchmarked instances.

The primary tradeoff of the c3.large is its reliance on legacy Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 hardware, which limits its computational efficiency compared to newer generations. While it offers dedicated CPU allocation and local NVMe SSD storage, its low memory capacity of 4.0 GB and poor memory bandwidth restrict its utility for modern memory-intensive applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a legacy hardware class with low resource density, making it suitable primarily for lightweight legacy workloads, basic single-threaded tasks, or small-scale testing environments that require dedicated CPU cores and local SSD storage but do not demand high memory or network throughput.
